title: Did you know… there was a king who sat in comfort while God’s Word was being read aloud—
paragraphs: Did you know… there was a king who sat in comfort while God’s Word was being read aloud—
…and as each section pierced the room…
And threw it into the fire.
The moment is recorded in Jeremiah 36.

God had spoken.
The scroll had been written.
The warning was clear.

The fire crackling beside him.
The air heavy.
The scroll unrolling slowly as it’s read.
And with every truth that got too close—
Until the entire Word of God…
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

You skipped that verse.
You ignored that conviction.
You silenced that voice telling you to stop.
Spiritual diagnosis: selective obedience rooted in hidden rebellion.
You don’t reject all of God’s Word.
Just the parts that confront you.
Listen to what God said about this moment:
“Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did they tear their garments.” — Jeremiah 36:24
But then comes the terrifying reality:
“The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.” — Isaiah 40:8

Not until you’re uncomfortable.
Not until culture changes.
Not until you disagree.
Because this isn’t just about a king long ago.
Or will you bow to it?
Because the same God who warned through Jeremiah—
also made a way through Jesus Christ.
You see, the scroll wasn’t just judgment.
A chance to turn before it was too late.
And today, that mercy is still extended to you:
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
Jesus didn’t come to be cut out of your life.
for the very sins you’re trying to hide.
“He was pierced for our transgressions… and by His wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
This is the moment Jehoiakim missed.
And let Jesus rewrite your story.
If this hit you, don’t ignore it.
